title: User force stop: zero callbacks, no drain, no epoch close; the next launch reports the last checkpoint

preconditions.notes: A task-manager stop is a SIGKILL plus a scheduling block: no lifecycle callback, no drain window and no epoch close can run, and the platform will not restart the process on its own.

timeline.event: three writes acked; one step open

timeline.detail: uncatchable and zero-callback: no Draining edge, no epoch close, no manifest rewrite, and no reschedule

timeline.event: nothing runs until the user opens the app again
timeline.detail: the platform blocks automatic restart after a task-manager stop
the persisted Running state maps to Recovering, boot disposition crash_recovery, admission closed

timeline.event: WAL scan and replay of the acked prefix
timeline.detail: every acked mseq is still present with the identical mutation

timeline.event: the interrupted epoch is reported to the user
timeline.detail: the Android runner must surface the interrupted step or turn on the next launch; the iOS baseline has no such surface, so this step is the Android equivalent added here

new_reason: Only surfaced_to_user is new: the iOS baseline has no user-visible report after a zero-callback stop (a killed process cannot publish, and no source path emits one on the next launch). The next-launch report is the Android equivalent required by the port plan, so the runner asserts it against this fixture, not against a Swift behaviour.
notes: Every durability expectation here is the same as kill-9; the reason the case exists separately is the scheduling block and the user-visible report. The Android free-stop path is SIGKILL, so nothing in this fixture may depend on a handler running.
